transcript: Brigadoon is one of my favourite musicals, so when I realised I would be in San Francisco while it was playing at the Pasadena Playhouse, it was an easy decision to drive down the coast. No, it was not a short drive, but let me tell you, this production was worth every mile. Brigadoon has just always captivated me. I love a sweeping romance. I love Scotland. It has some of my favourite musical theatre songs ever written. But I also recognise that Brigadoon, in a lot of ways, is very much of its time, like it debuted on Broadway in 1947. So when I Learned that Katie Spellman was going to be directing and choreographing it and that Alexandra Silber was going to be rewriting the book, I was so intrigued. It exceeded all of my expectations. Everything I love about Brigadoon is very much here, but so many elements have been thoughtfully reimagined. My favorite being at. The women of Brigadoon now have much more agency over their own life. Everything feels inspired and intentional. The characters feel more realized and more relevant, and the emotional stakes just hit harder. I just really loved every moment. My favorite part, though, might have been the choreography. The way that Katie Spellman story tells through movement is breathtaking. The big, splashy, joyful group numbers and one specific solo moment that had me weeping. Performances are equally incredible. For a few hours, I was completely immersed in this magical Scottish village. I felt pure whimsy and joy. And it's what I love the most about theatre. So if you get a chance, make your way to the Pasadena Playhouse. It's one of the most beautiful theatres in the country. They're always doing incredibly special work. And if you only get to see one production of Brigadoon every hundred years before it disappears into the mist, make it this one. It's worth the journey.
